name: Inkarnate
tagline: Browser based map maker for fantasy worlds, regions, cities and battle maps, built around a huge library of hand drawn art stamps.

pricing.basis: monthly, billed annually in most cases
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software part of Inkarnate is not the hard part. A layered canvas with a stamp brush, a texture ground brush, soft masking, text labels and PNG export is a well understood build, and an agent can get you something usable in a weekend. What you cannot one-shot is roughly ten thousand hand drawn, stylistically consistent art assets: mountains that tile with each other, forests that read at three zoom levels, trees that match the coastline textures. You can wire your build to free and CC0 asset packs and get real maps out of it, but they will look like a mix of five artists, because they are. The verdict is kinda because the editor survives the move and the art library does not.
coreLoopDIY: A local layered canvas editor where you paint ground textures with a soft brush and stamp PNG art assets at arbitrary scale and rotation, then export a flattened PNG.
requirements: Your own PNG asset packs, ideally CC0 or licensed, dropped into a folder
Patience for brush blending math, which is where the time goes
whatYouLose: The asset library, which is the actual product: thousands of stamps drawn in one coherent style
Style consistency, your DIY maps will visibly mix art sources
Polish like snapping, smart edge blending between biomes and the auto coastline look
Cloud saves and sharing maps by link
New asset drops every month that you did not have to draw
moatNotes: The moat is a commissioned art pipeline, not code. Every month of asset releases widens a gap that no coding agent closes.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a few dollars a month is nothing against drawing or licensing ten thousand consistent map assets yourself, and because the people buying this are usually GMs who want a map before Thursday, not a mapping engine. The editor is good enough and the art is the reason. If you are a competent artist with your own asset set, the calculus flips hard and a local build makes real sense.
notes: Build the editor, then spend your real weekend hunting CC0 stamp packs, that is the honest split.
prompt:
Build a local-only fantasy map editor as a single page web app. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript + react-konva for the canvas, Zustand for state, plain CSS. No UI component library.

Canvas model:
- Fixed map size chosen at new-map time, default 2048x1536, rendered scaled to fit with zoom and pan.
- Three layer types, stacked and reorderable: Ground (raster texture painting), Stamps (placed images), Labels (text).
- Multiple Ground layers so the user can paint grass, then dirt, then water on top.

Ground painting:
- Each Ground layer holds an offscreen canvas and a chosen tiling texture loaded from /public/textures.
- Brush paints the texture through a soft radial alpha mask using globalCompositeOperation, so strokes blend at the edges.
- Brush size slider, hardness slider, opacity slider, and an eraser mode on the same brush.

Stamps:
- Read /public/assets/manifest.json: an array of { id, name, category, file }. Build a searchable palette grouped by category.
- Click to place, drag to move, handles to scale and rotate. Scatter mode: holding the mouse down places randomly scaled and rotated copies along the drag path with a spacing setting.
- Flip horizontal, delete, bring forward, send back.

Labels: click to add text, drag to move, controls for font size, color, letter spacing, and a toggleable outline for legibility over busy terrain.

Persistence: save and load the whole map as a .map.json file through the File System Access API with a download fallback. Ground layers serialize as PNG data URLs. Also autosave to IndexedDB every 20 seconds and restore on load.

Export: flatten all layers to one PNG at full map resolution and download it.

Explicitly out of scope: multiplayer, VTT export, hex or square grids, lighting, fog of war, asset marketplace, any art assets. Ship 6 placeholder textures and 10 placeholder stamp PNGs generated as simple shapes, plus a README section explaining the manifest format so the user can drop in their own CC0 packs.

Deliver a working `npm run dev`, no .env needed since there are no secrets, and a README with the asset folder layout and a one-paragraph note that the app is useless without art.
